name: arm-pour
_: THE POUR, one turn of the clock: home → over the can → down and grip → lift → traverse → over the glass → 120° of tool roll → away. Eight waypoints solved by closed-form IK from task space, not posed by hand. The tip is a roll of the TOOL, because the can is held with its own axis perpendicular to the tool axis — which is also why ../gripper's one-way indexer could do this move itself. Six-DOF bench arm, counterweighted parallelogram. 250 + 250 + 60 mm of arm and 127 mm of tool, shoulder at z 400, reaching a 66 × 123 can at r 500. J2 and J3 are COAXIAL at the shoulder: J2 swings the upper arm and J3 a crank whose push rod drives an elbow crank rigid with the forearm, so the forearm's ABSOLUTE angle is j3 and nothing about j2 reaches it. Three things follow — both big actuators sit at the shoulder, gravity splits into two independent one-DOF problems, and a counterweight on each rear extension balances both EXACTLY at every pose, because load and counterweight go as the cosine of the same angle. 2.55 + 4.07 = 6.62 kg of steel (CW1 at r 300, CW2 as two pucks at r 200) takes 80% of it, leaving 1.88 N·m at J2 against 9.4 bare. Deliberately not 100%: a perfectly balanced arm drifts anywhere when the power dies, an 80% one settles downward.

base-plate._: Bench plate: Ø182 × 12, four M8 on a Ø144 circle into the bench. The whole machine's overturning moment lands here — 73 N·m of it with the arm out and the counterweights swung — so it is bolted down, not weighted down. One extrude along +Z.

column._: Column: Ø84 over Ø60, z 12…240. Hollow because the J1 harmonic's cabling and the whole arm's CAN bus run up the middle — a cable bundle outside a rotating joint is the thing that fails first. One extrude along +Z.

joint-small._: Actuator module stand-in, Ø50 × 45: the wrist's three. They see inertia and a little friction, nothing else — the tool's weight is reacted at the wrist centre, not by these.

can._: A 330 ml can, Ø66 × 123. Reference geometry — it is the task, not the machine.

pin._: Ø12 ground dowel through a parallelogram joint. One extrude along -Y.

assembly._: everything above the column, yawing with j1

turret._: J1 output plate: Ø92 × 14 on top of the column, carrying both shoulder cheeks. One extrude along +Z.

cheek._: Shoulder cheek, two off at |y| 74…86: they straddle the whole parallelogram and carry the COAXIAL J2 and J3 bores at z 400. Coaxial is the architecture — it is what puts the elbow's actuator at the shoulder and lets one counterweight per crank balance the arm exactly. `y1` is overridden per side. One extrude along -Y.

joint-large._: Actuator module stand-in, Ø80 × 70: NEMA 17 plus a 20:1 reduction, used at J2 and J3. Drawn along -Y; J1's instance is turned onto Z. The balanced J2 and J3 need 1.9 N·m against the 6.2 this delivers.

upper-arm._: Upper arm, J2 to the elbow, 250 mm, with a 300 mm rear extension carrying CW1. 60 × 20 on the centre plane. One extrude along -Y.

counterweight._: Counterweight: a plain steel cylinder Ø70 on a link's rear extension. CW1 is 2.55 kg (× 42.3 long) on the upper arm and CW2 4.07 kg (× 40.8) on the J3 cranks. Length is overridden per instance — the mass IS the tuning, and it is shimmable with washers. One extrude along -Y.

crank._: J3 crank, two off, coaxial with J2 and 80 mm long: the push rod hangs off its front end and CW2 off its 200 mm rear extension. The push rod delivers the forearm's whole gravitational moment here 1:1, which is exactly why a counterweight at this radius balances it at every angle. One extrude along -Y.

push-rod._: Push rod, two off, 250 mm — the same length as the upper arm and always parallel to it. That is the parallelogram: it makes the elbow crank parallel to the J3 crank, so the FOREARM'S ABSOLUTE ANGLE IS j3, whatever j2 does. One extrude along -Y.

elbow-crank._: Elbow crank, two off, 80 mm — the parallelogram's fourth bar, rigid with the forearm and reaching from its side face out under the push rod. One extrude along -Y.

forearm._: Forearm, elbow to the J4 roll section, 180 mm of a 250 mm reach. It carries no actuator: j3 arrives through the elbow crank from the shoulder. One extrude along -Y.

forearm-barrel._: Forearm barrel: Ø64 over Ø56, 80 long, swallowing the J4 motor and its reduction. The two forearm plates land on this instead of ending in mid-air. Ø64 and not Ø54 because a NEMA 17's DIAGONAL is 59.8. One extrude along +X.

nema17._: NEMA 17 stand-in: 42.3 square with 5 mm corner chamfers, 40 long. Two off — J4 coaxial up the forearm, J5 crosswise in the roll drum. One extrude along +X.

planetary._: Planetary reduction stand-in, Ø42 × 32. J4 takes 30:1 for its 5.57 N·m corner case; J5 takes only 10:1 because the belt is the other 3:1 — which is why the belt makes the gearbox cheaper, not dearer. One extrude along +X.

roll-bearing._: J4 bearing: Ø80 over Ø64, between the fixed barrel and the turning drum. It carries the whole wrist's cantilever — 5.6 N·m of it — so it is a crossed roller, like the gripper's. One extrude along +X.

assembly._: j4: the drum, the J5 drive inside it, the fork and the belt

roll-drum._: J4 roll drum: Ø118 over Ø110, turning with j4 and carrying the fork. It is this big because the J5 motor lies CROSSWISE inside it — that is the whole trick, and it is what takes the wrist's swept circle from Ø271 down to Ø118. The belt leaves through its open front face. One extrude along +X.

nema17._: NEMA 17 stand-in: 42.3 square with 5 mm corner chamfers, 40 long. Two off — J4 coaxial up the forearm, J5 crosswise in the roll drum. One extrude along +X.

planetary._: Planetary reduction stand-in, Ø42 × 32. J4 takes 30:1 for its 5.57 N·m corner case; J5 takes only 10:1 because the belt is the other 3:1 — which is why the belt makes the gearbox cheaper, not dearer. One extrude along +X.

pulley._: GT2 pulley at its PITCH diameter, drawn at ROOT diameter so the belt band clears it — the teeth we do not draw are what fills the 0.8 mm between them. Two off: 20T Ø12.73 on the J5 gearbox and 60T Ø38.2 on the pitch shaft. One extrude along -Y.

belt._: GT2 9 belt, 20T to 60T over 85 mm of centres — drawn as a real band so its envelope is a real clearance body, which the blade and the cheek both have to miss. One extrude along -Y.

fork-cheek._: J5 fork cheek, two off at |y| 29…39: carries the pitch bush at the wrist centre. `y1` is overridden per side. One extrude along -Y.

fork-web._: J5 fork web: the 58 mm spacer the two cheeks bolt to, closing the back of the slot and taking the roll tube's face. One extrude along -Y.

pitch-bush._: Flanged bush in a fork cheek, Ø22 outside on Ø16. Two off. One extrude along -Y.

assembly._: j5: the blade, its shaft, the driven pulley and the flange

wrist-blade._: J5 blade: the tool-side member, 54 thick between the fork's cheeks, bored on the pitch axis, and carrying its own Ø110 tool flange rather than a bolted-on plate. Through both runs a 44 square blind pocket, 48 deep — THE GRIPPER'S MOTOR LIVES IN HERE. That is what buys back the 54 mm the adapter cup used to cost: the actuator is behind the gripper's mounting face, so either the flange sits behind the motor or the wrist swallows it. Slab extruded along +Z, disc along +X, then the pocket and the pitch bore as cuts.

pitch-shaft._: Ø16 pitch shaft, pressed into the blade and running in a bush in each cheek. One extrude along -Y.

pulley._: GT2 pulley at its PITCH diameter, drawn at ROOT diameter so the belt band clears it — the teeth we do not draw are what fills the 0.8 mm between them. Two off: 20T Ø12.73 on the J5 gearbox and 60T Ø38.2 on the pitch shaft. One extrude along -Y.

cam-pod._: Wrist camera bracket: an L reaching from the flange disc's rear face out past the fork cheeks, holding a 16 square board camera looking DOWN the tool's −Z. It is on the blade, so J5 aims it and the hand-eye transform is a constant. It cannot see the grip point — nothing on the wrist can, with a Ø104 tool in front of it — and it does not pretend to: this is the camera that finds the can on the bench, not the one that watches the jaws close. One extrude along +Z, one pocket.

camera._: 16 × 16 × 10 board camera, looking along the tool's −Z. A 25 mm Pi Camera Module 3 would do the job optically and take the wrist's swept circle from Ø118 to Ø136; this class of module costs Ø5. The requirement is the envelope. One extrude along +Z.
